identity.what_it_is: A pebble beach on the base of a limestone cliff on the south-western coast of Lefkada island, Ionian Sea, Greece — reached historically by a metal staircase from a clifftop car park, and currently mainly by boat because land access is under a municipal closure order.
identity.where: South-western coast of Lefkada, Ionian Islands, Greece, near the village of Athani; ~39 km road from Lefkada Town, ~16 km from Vasiliki, ~37 km from Nydri.
identity.warnings: Name spelled variably as Egremni/Egremnoi/Egkremnoi across sources; all refer to the same beach. No distinct near-duplicate beach of the same name found in Greece.

spike_candidates.statement: The Municipality of Lefkada has kept Egremni's road and staircase under formal closure since 2025 for ground instability, yet boat operators advertise and dock there daily and a July 2025 visitor found the closure sign deliberately covered.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach the local government has declared legally off-limits is simultaneously sold as a headline stop on daily commercial boat tours, with no one taking responsibility if someone is hurt.

spike_candidates.statement: After February 2026 storms tore rockfall and bent railings into Egremni's staircase, it was cleared by an anonymous private initiative — by July 2026 no municipal engineer had inspected or certified the repair.
spike_candidates.tension: The only safety infrastructure standing between visitors and a 40-story rock descent is now maintained by volunteers, not the state that legally owns the beach.

spike_candidates.statement: The 2015 quake that destroyed Egremni's original 347-step staircase is often shrunk to a footnote in beach copy, but it was a 6.5-Mw event that killed two people elsewhere on Lefkada and buried the beach's sunbathing terrace under rockfall.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach's most-repeated backstory ("an earthquake changed everything") routinely drops the actual scale and human cost of the event that caused it.

spike_candidates.statement: Reaching Egremni today more often means a 12–40 euro boat from Vasiliki, a port only 16 km away, than the 37 km overland drive to Nydri that most guides still lead with.
spike_candidates.tension: The closer, cheaper departure point is underpublicized relative to the longer one that guides default to.

facts.fact: Egremni is on the south-western coast of Lefkada, an Ionian island in north-western Greece, at approximately 38°36'09"N 20°32'58"E.
facts.quote: Located on the south-western coast of Lefkada, an Ionian island in north-western Greece
facts.source_title: Egremni — Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach's name is transliterated inconsistently across English-language sources as Egremni, Egremnoi, or Egkremnoi; the Greek is Έγκρεμνοί.
facts.quote: Egremni (or Egremnoi) Beach
facts.source_title: Egremni (or Egremnoi) Beach — Lefkada Insider

facts.fact: A sealed road built in the mid-1990s turned Egremni from a remote spot into one of the island's premier tourist beaches before the 2015 earthquake.
facts.quote: Since the creation of a sealed road during the mid-1990s, this remote beach has become one of the premier tourist destinations on the island, and in Europe as a whole.
facts.source_title: Egremni — Wikipedia

facts.fact: Travel + Leisure listed Egremni among '13 Places Where You Can See the Bluest Water in the World.'
facts.quote: 13 Places Where You Can See the Bluest Water in the World
facts.source_title: Egremni — Wikipedia

facts.fact: Before the 2015 earthquake, Egremni's only descent was a mountain path of 347 steep steps.
facts.quote: 347 steep steps
facts.source_title: Egremni — Wikipedia

facts.fact: The Lefkada earthquake struck on 17 November 2015 at 10:40 EEST with a moment magnitude of 6.5.
facts.quote: November 17, 2015, at 10:40:07 EEST; 6.5 moment magnitude (Mw)
facts.source_title: 2015 Lefkada earthquake — Wikipedia

facts.fact: The 2015 earthquake killed two elderly women on Lefkada — a 69-year-old hit by a boulder that struck her house, and an 82-year-old killed by a collapsing wall.
facts.quote: A 69-year-old woman died when a boulder from a loose mountain had hit her house... an 82-year-old woman also died when a wall collapsed onto her.
facts.source_title: 2015 Lefkada earthquake — Wikipedia

facts.fact: A flank of the Egremni cliff collapsed in the 2015 earthquake, burying the former sunbathing terrace in rubble; because it happened in winter, the beach was unoccupied at the time.
facts.quote: A flank of the well-known pristine Egremni Beach collapsed following the massive tremor.
facts.source_title: Earth Swallows One of Greece's Most Beautiful Beaches — GreekReporter

facts.fact: The site's existing overview draft states the 2015 quake was '5.1 magnitude,' which conflicts with the 6.5 Mw figure recorded by seismological sources — the draft figure appears to be an invented/incorrect number.
facts.quote: 6.5 moment magnitude (Mw)
facts.source_title: 2015 Lefkada earthquake — Wikipedia

facts.fact: In November 2019, Lefkada mayor Charalambos Kalos announced the road to Egremni would reopen for the coming tourist season, with rebuild work targeted for completion by late February 2020.
facts.quote: Mayor Charalambos Kalos announced in November 2019 that the road would open for the summer tourist season, with work completion targeted for late February 2020
facts.source_title: Κλειστή για πέμπτο συνεχόμενο καλοκαίρι η οδική πρόσβαση στην παραλία «Εγκρεμνοί» — Λευκαδίτικα Νέα

facts.fact: The COVID-19 pandemic delayed the originally planned early-2020 completion of the Egremni access rebuild.
facts.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the original timeline
facts.source_title: Κλειστή για πέμπτο συνεχόμενο καλοκαίρι — Λευκαδίτικα Νέα

facts.fact: By June 2020 a specialized Slovenian aerial-work crew had arrived to install pre-assembled sections of the new staircase, with officials estimating 30-45 more days to finish.
facts.quote: A specialized Slovenian aerial work crew had arrived to install pre-assembled staircase sections. Officials estimated 30-45 days for completion
facts.source_title: Κλειστή για πέμπτο συνεχόμενο καλοκαίρι — Λευκαδίτικα Νέα

facts.fact: As of June 2020, road access to Egremni had been closed for five consecutive summers running (i.e., every summer since the 2015 quake).
facts.quote: Κλειστή για πέμπτο συνεχόμενο καλοκαίρι η οδική πρόσβαση στην παραλία «Εγκρεμνοί»
facts.source_title: Κλειστή για πέμπτο συνεχόμενο καλοκαίρι — Λευκαδίτικα Νέα

facts.fact: By 12 May 2021, Egremni had become road-accessible again after 6 years, with roughly 420 new steps and the new staircase in place, about 40 km from Lefkada town.
facts.quote: γύρω στα 420 (!) σκαλοπάτια; Η οδική πρόσβαση έχει ήδη αποκατασταθεί, η καινούργια σκάλα έχει τοποθετηθεί; 40 περίπου χιλιόμετρα έξω από την πόλη της Λευκάδας
facts.source_title: Εγκρεμνοί: Η ωραιότερη παραλία της Ελλάδας ξανά προσβάσιμη μετά από 6 χρόνια — Έθνος

facts.fact: The rebuild of the road and steps to Egremni, completed by summer 2021, was described by local press as an especially difficult job primarily because of the safety demands of the site.
facts.quote: the renovation of the road and steps was a very challenging job, primarily because of safety
facts.source_title: Road to Egremni beach is finally finished — Nikana.gr

facts.fact: Following a fresh geological risk assessment, the Municipality of Lefkada formally closed road and land access to Egremni again starting in 2025, citing severe ground instability; the closure remains legally in force.
facts.quote: the Municipality of Lefkada formally closed the road and land access to Egremni Beach since 2025 due to severe ground instability
facts.source_title: Is Egremni Beach Open? Important Safety Update for 2026 Visitors — Vasiliki.eu

facts.fact: On 25 February 2026, heavy rain caused rockfall that damaged the Egremni staircase near its base and blocked the path, according to reports and tourist video from the scene.
facts.quote: Εγκρεμνοί Λευκάδας: Αναφορές για ζημιές στη σκάλα πρόσβασης μετά τις βροχές
facts.source_title: Εγκρεμνοί Λευκάδας: Αναφορές για ζημιές στη σκάλα πρόσβασης μετά τις βροχές — Lefkada Today

facts.fact: As of the February 2026 storm damage, the Egremni staircase reportedly had gone roughly four years without maintenance or an engineering inspection by municipal personnel.
facts.quote: the staircase appears to lack maintenance and inspection [from municipal engineers] over the extended period
facts.source_title: Εγκρεμνοί Λευκάδας — Lefkada Today

facts.fact: By 1 July 2026, a private (non-municipal) initiative had cleared the fallen rocks and repaired bent railings on the staircase, but no city engineer had issued any official statement on the safety or structural integrity of that work — the tourism authority instead recommends boat access from Vasiliki.
facts.quote: the steps have now been cleared of the fallen stones and the bent railings; there has been no official statement from the authorities regarding the safety or structural integrity of these repairs
facts.source_title: Is Egremni Beach Open? Important Safety Update for 2026 Visitors — Vasiliki.eu

facts.fact: A visitor who went to Egremni in early July 2025 reported that the sign prohibiting entry had been covered or hidden and that a closed vehicle gate had a small gap allowing people through, with debris still visible on the beach and an untransparent €10-per-car parking charge collected with no receipt.
facts.quote: Στους Εγγεμνούς έχουν κρύψει-σκεπάσει τη ταμπέλα που απαγορεύει την είσοδο; Πήγαμε αρχές Ιουλίου 2025 στη Λευκάδα
facts.source_title: Νιώθω την ανάγκη να εκφράσω δημόσια την απογοήτευσή μου... — aromalefkadas.gr

facts.fact: The harbor authority has fielded complaints from swimmers about debris and rubble falling on the beach during ongoing restoration, while boat operators continue to advertise and dock at Egremni despite its official closed status — leaving unresolved who is liable if someone is hurt.
facts.quote: boats advertise Egremni in their brochures and transport visitors, yet authorities classify it as closed and inform bathers to leave
facts.source_title: Οι Εγκρεμνοί σαν παραλία παραμένουν κλειστοί ή όχι; — Lefkada Today

facts.fact: By road, Egremni is about 39 km from Lefkada Town, 16 km from Vasiliki, 37 km from Nydri, and 4 km from the village of Athani.
facts.quote: about 39 kilometres from Lefkada town; 16 kilometres from Vasiliki; 37 kilometres from Nidri; 4 kilometres from the village of Athani
facts.source_title: Egremni Beach — Where it is located and how to get there — Visit Greece Info

facts.fact: Egremni and its neighbor Porto Katsiki are about 4 km apart by road, roughly a 5-minute drive.
facts.quote: The distance between Egremni Beach and Porto Katsiki is 2.6 miles or 4 km
facts.source_title: Distance between Egremni Beach and Porto Katsiki

facts.fact: From the clifftop car park, visitors face roughly a 1.5 km sloped walk to the top of the staircase, then a 420-step metal staircase with a 30-40 minute descent and up to an hour's climb back up in heat.
facts.quote: 420-step metal staircase rebuilt in 2021; Descent time: 30-40 minutes downward; Ascent time: Up to one hour
facts.source_title: Egremni Beach — Visit Greece Info

facts.fact: There is a simple taverna/snack bar at the top of the Egremni staircase selling drinks and snacks; beach-level sunbed/umbrella rental and a small snack stand operate seasonally (roughly June-September) and vary year to year.
facts.quote: a simple taverna serving cool drinks and snacks; seasonal sunbed and umbrella rentals (June through September), and sometimes a small bar / snack stand at the bottom of the stairs (varies seasonally)
facts.source_title: Egremni Beach, Lefkada: 2026 Guide To Stairs, Parking & Access — Drink Tea & Travel

facts.fact: Vasiliki Daily Cruise (Explore Lefkada) runs a daily boat trip from Vasiliki port stopping at Egremni, priced at €40 for adults and €20 for children 6-12 (lunch +€10), departing 10:00 AM and returning 18:00-18:30, with the operator's booking page live for the 2026 season and a listed capacity of up to 200 passengers.
facts.quote: EGREMNI BEACH; 40€ / Person; Book your ticket for the best experience in Lefkada from Vasiliki port for 2026!
facts.source_title: Vasiliki Daily Cruise — Explore Lefkada

facts.fact: Water taxis from the small port of Vasiliki to Porto Katsiki and Egremni are advertised at around €12 per person for the Egremni leg.
facts.quote: Two water taxis depart from the small port of Vassiliki to Porto Katsiki and Egremni, with costs around 12€ for Egremni
facts.source_title: Lefkada Water Taxis Routes & Services — Greeka

facts.fact: A separate operator runs an 8-hour boat cruise from Nydri to Egremni, Porto Katsiki, and Agiofili, listed live on GetYourGuide for the 2026 season at roughly $41-51 per person with free cancellation.
facts.quote: NYDRI: Cruise to Egremni, Porto Katsiki, Agiofili of Lefkada
facts.source_title: NYDRI: Cruise to Egremni, Porto Katsiki, Agiofili of Lefkada — GetYourGuide

facts.fact: Vertzami, a rare red-wine grape grown at 200-700 m altitude, has dominated Lefkada's mountain vineyards since Venetian times and produces the island's best-regarded red wine.
facts.quote: Grapes of the rare Vertzami type are grown at altitudes of 200 to 700 meters, from which the best wine in Lefkada is made... has dominated vineyards in Lefkada's mountain range since Venetian times.
facts.source_title: Local products in Lefkada — Nikana.gr

facts.fact: Frigadeli, a Lefkada specialty, is lamb liver wrapped in lamb caul and grilled on a spit like souvlaki; the name is said to derive from Italian words for liver.
facts.quote: Frigadeli consists of pieces of lamb liver covered in lamb wrap lined up in a spit and usually grilled like the usual Greek souvlaki.
facts.source_title: Local products in Lefkada — Nikana.gr

facts.fact: Other named Lefkada specialties include the lentils of Englouvi village, an island air-dried salami, and local pastels and nougat sweets, plus olive oil and honey from the interior.
facts.quote: famous lentils of Englouvi, special Lefkada air salami, and from sweets, pastels and nougat
facts.source_title: Local products in Lefkada — Nikana.gr

facts.fact: Under Greek law, the shoreline (αιγιαλός) is public property belonging to the State, which is responsible for its protection and management — the legal basis for the Municipality's authority to close or restrict access at Egremni.
facts.quote: the beach and shoreline are public property, belong to the ownership of the State, which protects and manages them
facts.source_title: Αιγιαλός: ορισμοί, κυριότητα, παραχώρηση απλής χρήσης — dasarxeio.com

facts.fact: There is no lifeguard service at Egremni; multiple current visitor guides describe it as swim-at-your-own-risk, with steep pebble entry and quick drop-offs offshore.
facts.quote: no lifeguard service
facts.source_title: Egremni Beach, Lefkada — Drink Tea & Travel

facts.fact: Sources disagree on the exact step count for the staircase and clifftop distances, but converge on a range: 300-420 steps and a car-park-to-stairs walk of 1-1.5 km, indicating the numbers vary by which construction phase (pre- or post-2021) a given source describes.
facts.quote: approximately 400 metal stairs (sources cite 350-420 range)
facts.source_title: Egremni Beach, Lefkada — Drink Tea & Travel

facts.fact: The beach dataset's straight-line distances (15.3 km to Nidri, 36.8 km to PVK airport) are far shorter than the actual road distances sourced above (37 km to Nydri, and no verified official PVK road figure), reflecting Lefkada's winding coastal roads rather than any error.
facts.quote: 37 kilometres from Nidri
facts.source_title: Egremni Beach — Visit Greece Info

recency.newest_item: As of 1 July 2026 (vasiliki.eu safety update), the Egremni staircase — storm-damaged in February 2026 — had been cleared of rocks and bent railings by a private, non-municipal initiative, but no city engineer had inspected or certified the repair, and the local tourism authority was steering visitors to boat access from Vasiliki instead of the stairs.

dead_ends: No film, TV show, song, or book was found that names Egremni explicitly; no verifiable cultural reference exists for the culture section.

No news report, official record, or lifeguard/coast-guard statement documenting a specific named drowning or rescue incident at Egremni was found (only general Greek national beach-drowning statistics for 2025, not beach-specific).

No official government or airport source gives a road driving distance or drive time from PVK (Aktion) airport to Egremni or to Nydri; all such figures (e.g. '50-60 minutes') appear only in unofficial travel-guide sites and could not be sourced to an official operator.

No confirmed grouper/octopus or other specific marine-life claim for Egremni's waters was found in any source — the existing overview.mdx claim about 'grouper and octopus in deeper zones' is unverified and should be treated as unsupported.

No official parking-fee schedule was found; sources conflict between free parking (30-50 cars) and a paid ~€4-10/day lot, and a 2025 visitor report of an off-the-books €10 cash charge with no receipt — there is no single authoritative current price.
No official beach length or substrate figure exists beyond the beach dataset's own 'unknown' fields; no source gave a specific beach length in meters.
conflicts: Earthquake magnitude: the site's existing overview.mdx draft states '5.1 magnitude' earthquake in 2015; Wikipedia's dedicated earthquake article gives 6.5 Mw at 10:40 EEST on 17 November 2015 (F06, F09). The 6.5 figure is the sourced one.
Distance Egremni-Porto Katsiki: overview.mdx says 5 km; distancebetween.info gives 4 km road distance (F23).

Staircase step count: cited variously as 347 (original, pre-2015, Wikipedia F05), ~420 (post-2021 rebuild, Ethnos F14), and 'approximately 400' or '300-420' in general guides (F34) — the discrepancy tracks the pre- vs post-earthquake construction, not a single wrong number.

Parking: some sources describe a free 30-50 car clifftop lot; visit-greece.info describes a paid ~€10 lot 1.5 km from the stairs; a 2025 visitor reports an informal €10 cash charge with no receipt at a rear lot (F20, F24, F25) — no single current authoritative price exists.

Access framing: overview.mdx and travel.mdx present the rebuilt staircase as a live, semi-normal access option with boat tours as the 'preferred' alternative; current 2025-2026 sources establish that land access is under an active municipal closure order and the staircase is uninspected/uncertified since February 2026 storm damage — boat is now effectively the only sanctioned way in (F16, F19, F21).
